findings.effort: A column in stops.txt; your scheduling software likely has it.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_boarding to 1 (accessible) or 2 (not accessible) for every stop. A field survey can start with the busiest stops.
findings.what: 155 of 155 stops don't say whether a wheelchair user can board there.
findings.why: Riders who use wheelchairs can't plan a trip when accessibility is marked 'unknown'; apps show no information at all.

findings.effort: A default or per-trip field in your export.
findings.fix: Set wheelchair_accessible on every trip. If every vehicle is accessible, this may be one default; otherwise use the value for each trip.
findings.what: 407 of 407 trips don't say whether the vehicle is wheelchair accessible.
findings.why: Even with accessible stops, riders need to know the bus itself can take them.

findings.effort: Usually one value per route pattern in your scheduling source.
findings.fix: Add the destination, direction, or 'via' label riders actually see to trip_headsign. Do not copy the route name. If the label changes during the trip, use stop_headsign.
findings.what: 130 of 407 trips lack rider-facing destination or direction text.
findings.why: When a route has multiple directions or patterns, the route name alone may not tell riders which service is coming.

findings.effort: A small file; one rule often covers the whole service.
findings.fix: Add booking_rules.txt saying how far ahead and how to book (phone, app, or web).
findings.what: This feed describes flexible (demand-responsive) service but has no booking_rules.txt.
findings.why: Riders can see the service area but not how or when to reserve a trip, so they can't actually use the service.

completeness.summary: 0% of stops state wheelchair accessibility (0% marked accessible, 0% marked not accessible). This measures what the feed publishes, not whether a stop is physically usable. Fare data is published.

findings.effort: A review pass in your scheduling software.
findings.fix: Remove retired stops from the export, or add them back to the trips that should serve them.
findings.what: Some stops exist in the feed but no trip ever stops at them.
findings.why: Riders may walk to a stop where no bus is scheduled to arrive.

findings.effort: A quick look at the flagged files.
findings.fix: Check the flagged column names for misspellings of standard GTFS fields; remove them if they are vendor extras.
findings.what: Some files contain columns that are not part of the GTFS spec.
findings.why: Harmless to riders, but apps ignore these columns and they can hide typos in real column names.

findings.effort: A quick look at the flagged file.
findings.fix: Check the flagged file name for a typo of a standard GTFS file. Remove it if it is a vendor extra.
findings.what: The feed includes a file that is not part of the GTFS spec.
findings.why: Apps ignore files they don't know, and a stray file can hide a misspelled standard file name.

findings.effort: Two fields in feed_info.txt, or one export setting.
findings.fix: Widen feed_start_date and feed_end_date to cover all service dates, or fix the dates that fall outside.
findings.what: Some service dates fall outside the date window set in feed_info.txt.
findings.why: feed_info.txt should span every day your service runs, so apps know when the data applies.

ntd_id_alignment.detail: Your feed's agency_id is 526; your National Transit Database ID is 90165. A feed that serves several agencies (a shared regional feed) can legitimately carry more than one agency_id. The values do not need to equal the five-digit NTD ID, so this difference is allowed and carries no score.
ntd_id_alignment.fix: Confirm that P-50 crosswalks agency_id 526 to NTD ID 90165, and keep the feed value stable. Do not change it solely to make the two values equal.

pillars.detail: Service data covers the next 149 days.
agency.txt provides agency_id. For RY2026, keep one stable value for each NTD reporter represented in the feed and crosswalk each value on the P-50 form.

recommendations.effort: A small file; one rule often covers the whole service.
recommendations.fix: Add booking_rules.txt with how far ahead and how to reserve (phone, app, or web).
recommendations.what: Flex zones are published but no booking_rules.txt is present.
recommendations.why: Riders can see the service area but not how to book, so they can't complete a trip.

recommendations.effort: A per-route color setting in your scheduling software.
recommendations.fix: Adjust route_color or route_text_color so each pair clears 4.5:1. Often switching the text between black and white is enough.
recommendations.what: 4 route badge(s) pair a color and text color below the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast bar (Route 40, Route 41, Route 45, Beach Bus).
recommendations.why: Low-contrast route badges are hard to read for riders with low vision and wash out on a phone screen in sunlight at the stop.

recommendations.effort: A short text field per affected stop; start with the busiest.
recommendations.fix: Add tts_stop_name with the spoken form, e.g. 'Main Street and Second Avenue', for the affected stops.
recommendations.what: 140 stop name(s) use abbreviations or symbols a screen reader may mispronounce, with no spoken form set ("Teller Road west of Lawrence Dr. (W/B)", "Janss Rd. & Montgomery Rd..", "Janss Rd. at Conejo Valley High School.", and more).
recommendations.why: Riders who use a screen reader hear the raw name, so 'Main St & 2nd Ave' can come out as 'Main saint' or drop the ampersand.

findings.effort: A cleanup pass in your scheduling software.
